utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Please be seated. Madam Registrar, may I please ask you to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-01-42-A, the Prosecutor versus Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution, Mark McKeon. To my right is my co-counsel, Mr. Xavier Tracol and to my left is our case manager, Victoria McCreath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I appear on behalf of General Strugar. My name is Goran Rodic, attorney at law from Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Strugar, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Whilst you just have the floor, may I ask you at this time only whether you have any complaints about the conditions in the United Nations Detention Unit? I want on purpose to split the question and come back to the question of your health later on during this Status Conference. Do you have any complaints? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Applying Rule 65 ter, together with Rule 107, of course, obliges the Appeals Chamber and the Pre-Appeal Judge to try to hear this case as expeditiously as possible, and on my own agenda, I have foreseen that we discuss today questions of filings, questions of health, and then how to streamline the case. So let us start with the filings. I think we received most of the filings. In any event, all of the filings that are due until today. There was a request by the Defence for extension of time. Please correct me if I'm wrong, is the translation into B/C/S was filed the 13th of June 2005, meaning that the Defence, Appellant's brief, as such, is due on 8 July 2005. Are there any other filings due or to be expected, in particular filings under Rule 115 on additional evidence? Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point in time, the Defence will not be filing anything like that. Likewise, there is no additional evidence at this point in time. We are still investigating regardless of the judgement. This is of course related to difficulties regarding where we come from, both in terms of evidence and in terms of witnesses. As soon as we have something new, we shall of course go to the Chamber and alert the Chamber immediately should there be any new evidence emerging in due time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you have seen the development in the jurisprudence of the Appeals Chamber being more and more reluctant with the admission of additional evidence since the files have been opened in nearly the entire former Yugoslavia and there is in principle no need for additional evidence but of course this rule exists and if you find something, please alert us well in advance, that we can deal with this case as expeditiously as possible. But may I ask you one question? You filed the 27th June 2005 your Defence response brief. This file was filed confidential. Is there any purpose behind this? And if so -- if need may be, we could go into private session for an explanation or -- please understand that it was only possible for me to have a kind of perusal of this document but I can't see something which warrants to have this document as a confidential one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in compliance with the confidential nature of the document, can we go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is there any plan by the Prosecution to file any motion under Rule 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We have no such plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's discuss the development of this case. As I said beforehand, it's our duty and in this case as a Pre-Appeal Judge, my own duty, to take care that the exchanges between the parties and everything around this takes place in a way that ensures expeditious preparation of the appeal. I have to tell you that as things stand now, on the waiting list for appeals, the case here in the ICTY, it's called Prosecutor versus Strugar, it would be the other way around in the ICTY, he is under number 11 of the cases to be heard. But at the same time, there is a substantial likelihood that three appeal judgements would be rendered in due course, that de facto it would be number 8, but this does not mean that in fact it's the 8th case in line. We will all try, and we shall try all our very best, that we hear the case as soon as possible and is therefore always the attempt to stick to the time limits as foreseen in the rules. I appreciate that in all likelihood, as things stand now, there will be no 115 motion and we can proceed as soon as possible the moment we have all necessary filings under the rules, the response and reply. In order to streamline the appeal and also, as the appeals brief, as such, is still to be expected, may I give, as it is tradition in not only in civil law systems, some judicial hints to the Defence? Please don't misunderstand those hints as any attempt to limit your brief. However, I was a little bit concerned when reading the notice of appeal. I saw several times that the Defence asserts that all factual and legal findings which permitted the Trial Chamber to find the accused Pavle Strugar guilty of any offence were in error. You should be aware that it's settled jurisprudence of the Trial Chamber that such a catch-all clause would constitute an insufficient pleading, as not each and every error of fact and/or law will lead to a miscarriage of justice or invalidate the decision respectively. All these errors have and the question whether they lead -- it leads to a miscarriage of justice or invalidation of the decision, has to be precisely demonstrated by the appealing party. Thus, the Appellant's brief has to be extremely specific in this respect. And the same is true in relation to other of your 100 reasons of appeal. I would give also the judicial hint that you allege that there were alleged errors of fact based on the lack of corroboration. I only want to recall that it is the consistent jurisprudence of the ICTY that no corroboration is required at all, save under certain circumstances, but those would have to be explained in all detail. And then the final judicial hint would be: As regards errors of fact, the threshold is extremely high and you should be aware that only where the events -- evidence relied on by the Trial Chamber could not have been accepted by any reasonable trier of fact, or where the evaluation of the evidence is wholly erroneous, may the Appeals Chamber substitute its own finding for that of the Trial Chamber. This is only to alert you on the limits we have in our work, and maybe already, based on these hints, you may consider or reconsider the question whether upholding one or other reason of appeal. It's custom whenever I'm acting as a Pre-Appeal Judge that I not only give these hints but also to -- having been myself Defence counsel, asking the Defence to focus on the real elements of concern of the Defence, because sometimes it has happened that by too many reasons of appeal, you hide and you refrain, and you let us refrain from looking on the focus or having the focus on those elements and those errors you believe are the most important ones. And therefore, it's always in favour of the Defence and, of course, of Mr. Strugar himself, that we focus on the central issues of the case. Let me state in this connection that I'm always prepared to have an in-camera meeting between all the parties in my office, applying Rule 65 ter (D)(iv) in conjunction with Rule 107, maybe to settle the one or other dispute beforehand, that we then later, when it comes to the appeal hearing, can really focus on the central points of both appeals. Please don't hesitate to alert me if the one or the other or both parties want to have such a meeting. Otherwise, it may be that the Appeals Chamber proprio motu takes this measure. Are there any other questions related to the filings and speeding up of the appeal? The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your advice, Your Honour. If there is anything I can do to clarify the situation in relation to the appeal, as you defined it, the appeal is certain to focus on the subject matter that you have just spoken about. There will be four or five groups of arguments to our appeal. As far as that's concerned, I don't think there will be any problems. Likewise, I wish to thank you for being so prepared to help us with organising meetings outside the Status Conferences that will be scheduled. The Defence shall have further motions in that respect in all likelihood. As for all the other issues, the Defence would like to raise one particular issue that you have referred to. I'm talking about General Strugar's health, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you? We will come to the let at the final point. Let's first discuss the filings on the subject matter of the case and the health will be later -- at a later stage in this hearing, and in all likelihood in private session. May I ask the Prosecution is there any problem in relation to filings in the future and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. any initiative to speed up proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. At this point we don't anticipate any problems. We will have to wait and see how the appeal brief looks to see whether there are any problems generated by that, in terms of our response in a timely fashion. But at there point we don't anticipate anything and we will certainly consider any ways that we might speed up the process and will bring them to the Court's attention if we have any suggestions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this and I can only tell you and of course both parties that time limits, they indicate only the maximum of the time, and, of course, the Appeals Chamber would appreciate if you could come with a response or reply even earlier than foreseen in the time limits in our Rules. Let's leave it with this for today, but then let's go to a more specific point and let's please go for this purpose as we want to discuss private issues, like the health condition of the Appellant in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. This concludes this Status Conference.
